menu_restore: Send sound and light again when plugged in
about_text: Controls the Maono PD200X and PD200XS on Linux: gain, monitoring, noise cancellation, EQ, compressor, limiter and the ring light, plus the system's microphone volume above 100 % (PipeWire).
about_license: License: GPL-3.0 · © Tristan Teufel and contributors. The USB protocol follows pd200x by advnpzn (MIT).
about_trademark: MAONO and PD200X are trademarks of their owner. This project is not affiliated with MAONO.
banner_notFound_text: Plug the microphone in over USB. The app connects by itself.
banner_permission_text: Linux does not let your user control the microphone yet. Install the udev rule from the packaging folder (or the .deb/.rpm package, which brings it) and plug the microphone in again:
basics_gain_max: Hardware at its maximum. Only the system's microphone volume gives more.
basics_boost_kde: the same control as in your system's sound settings
calibrate_intro: Speak for {seconds} seconds the way you usually do, for example a sentence from your day. The app then proposes gain and microphone volume so your peaks land near −9 dB. Nothing changes until you agree.
sound_profiles_hint: The microphone's 8 profiles, plus your own
sound_eq_hint: Drag the points: left/right = frequency, up/down = level, mouse wheel = Q
profile_new_text: Saves the current equalizer under a name.
light_linkage_hint: Shows at a glance whether people can hear you. Does not apply while the ring is off.
light_note: The app reads colour, brightness and sound from the microphone when it connects. Only “light off while muted” is remembered by the app.
light_preview_label: Preview: the microphone on its arm with the ring light in the chosen colour
error_notFound: No PD200X found. Is it plugged in over USB?
error_permissionDenied: No permission for the microphone. The udev rule is missing.
error_noAudioSource: PipeWire does not know the microphone as an input.
error_toolMissing: wpctl or pw-dump is missing (PipeWire tools).
error_noVoice: No voice heard. Speak normally into the microphone while measuring.
